newsitem.title: USA: CBOT, CME release audit trail data to CFTC.
newsitem.headline: CBOT, CME release audit trail data to CFTC.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade and Chicago Mercantile Exchange have sent audit trail data to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, as the CFTC had requested last summer, a commission spokesman said.
"We've received data from the Chicago exchanges and we are currently evaluating the data," he said.

The CFTC required both exchanges to demonstrate by January 1, 1997 that they had achieved a 90 percent verifiability rate in the time and sequence of trades. The CFTC concluded in its August 1996 status report on U.S. exchange audit trails that neither exchange had met new, heightened standards.
Carol Burke, CBOT executive vice president and general counsel, said the CBOT is confident its data will demonstrate the exchange's compliance.
"It gave us an opportunity to adopt additional measures to improve our compliance," Burke said at a CBOT news briefing.
CME officials were unavailable for comment. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
